      About

      I’m still early in learning to be an engineer, and I like it best when I get to follow something from a first sketch all the way to a test.

      I’m an aerospace engineering student at Stanford. Last summer I worked as a mechanical and materials engineering intern at SpaceX on Starship, and I’m returning to the same role in summer 2027. Most of what I took away from it was how much there is still to learn.

      A lot of how I think about design comes from four seasons as hardware lead and project manager on FTC Team 4545. I designed our mechanisms in CAD, machined and printed the parts, and learned to iterate: one claw prong went through 12 versions before it could correct its own alignment, and an intake took 15 before it worked 98% of the time. That habit of testing, being wrong and trying again has followed me into CFD research on engine placement and the BAE Systems FOCUS rover challenge, where I led the mechanical design.

      I also love writing software. I’ve been building Poise, a posture and eye-break coach for Mac and iPhone that uses AirPods head tracking, and I’ve written C++, Java and Python for microcontrollers, robots and small tools.

      Some of the work I care about most is helping other students get started. I co-founded FolioLearning, a STEM nonprofit, and mentored new robotics teams in three countries through the LaunchPad Initiative.
